newsitem.title: TURKEY: Arafat slams Jerusalem housing plan.
newsitem.headline: Arafat slams Jerusalem housing plan.

text.p: Palestinian president Yasser Arafat on Wednesday slammed Israel's plan to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem and said it would push the Middle East peace process into a corner.
"The settlement is completely illegal and it is against the U.N. conclusions and the agreements which we signed," Arafat told reporters on his arrival in Ankara for a one-day visit.

"So to continue this policy will push the peace process into the corner and we will face many difficulties. I am completely against it," said Arafat, who will meet Turkish officials, including President Suleyman Demirel and Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, before leaving Ankara on Thursday.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu went to parliament earlier on Wednesday for talks with government and opposition deputies over plans to build the neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem, which Palestinians regard as the capital of their future state. Israel views all Jerusalem as its capital.
The plan is to construct 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa, a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel in 1967.
Right-wing coalition partners and several members of the main opposition Labour party have been pressing Netanyahu to give the green light for the construction.
Nabil Shaath, minister of planning and international cooperation in the Palestinian Authority, said the plan would jeapordise the peace process.
"The building of a new settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim is dangerous and will have dire consequences on the (peace) process," Shaath said after meeting Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa in Cairo.
"It will create an Israeli presence and is a violation of Palestinian rights in the final status of that area," he added.

Critics said the plan would spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gunbattles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.
